# Citation

An inline citation marker, such as a superscript 1 after a sentence, that shows its source on hover or focus.
Markdown renders `[1]` as a Citation when it is given `sources`.

**Interaction**: hovering or focusing it with `Tab` shows a popover with the title, the site and the description
of the source, and leaving or `Esc` hides it; it does not move focus. With a safe address the marker is a link
to the source (other sites open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`); otherwise it is a button that
only shows the popover. Screen readers read "Source 1: title".

**Category**: AI · **Common uses**: Numbered citations in AI answers, footnote-style references in generated text

## Import

```ts
import { Citation } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

Place a Citation after the sentence it supports. Hover it or focus it with `Tab` to see the source; the number
links to it.

```tsx
import { Citation, type SourceItem, Text } from 'vellum-ui'

const SOURCES: readonly SourceItem[] = [
  {
    title: 'Shipping small releases',
    url: 'https://www.example.com/blog/shipping-small',
    description: 'Why teams that release weekly find problems earlier, and how to start.',
  },
  {
    title: 'Release checklist template',
    url: 'https://docs.example.org/templates/release',
    description: 'A one-page checklist covering scope, tests, notes and rollback.',
  },
]

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Text as="p">
      Smaller releases make problems easier to find
      <Citation index={1} source={SOURCES[0] as SourceItem} />, and a short checklist keeps them
      consistent
      <Citation index={2} source={SOURCES[1] as SourceItem} />.
    </Text>
  )
}
```

## Advanced

### In Markdown

Give Markdown the `sources` and it renders `[1]`, `[2]` in the reply as citations; put the list under the reply
with Sources.

```tsx
import { Markdown, type SourceItem, Sources, Stack } from 'vellum-ui'

const SOURCES: readonly SourceItem[] = [
  {
    title: 'Shipping small releases',
    url: 'https://www.example.com/blog/shipping-small',
    description: 'Why teams that release weekly find problems earlier, and how to start.',
  },
  {
    title: 'Release checklist template',
    url: 'https://docs.example.org/templates/release',
    description: 'A one-page checklist covering scope, tests, notes and rollback.',
  },
]

export function InMarkdown() {
  return (
    <Stack gap={3}>
      <Markdown
        sources={SOURCES}
        content={
          'Release **weekly** if you can [1]. Use one checklist for every release [2], and keep it short. [3] has no source, so it stays as text.'
        }
      />
      <Sources items={SOURCES} />
    </Stack>
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | `number` | The number shown, usually the position of the source in Sources (starting at 1). | — | Yes |
| `source` | `SourceItem` | The source it refers to. | — | Yes |

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.

## Types

Types of this library used above. Import them with `import type { … } from 'vellum-ui'`.

### SourceItem

One source of Sources and Citation.

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable key; the index is used when omitted. | — | No |
| `title` | `string` | Title of the page or document. | — | Yes |
| `url` | `string` | Address. Only http, https, mailto and relative addresses become links (others are shown as text); the site name is taken from it. | — | No |
| `description` | `string` | A short excerpt or summary. | — | No |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | An icon for the site, provided by the application (such as an image from its own server). Remote site icons are never loaded automatically. | — | No |
